Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Controls and discrete intents

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Movement, aim, held fire and revive use sampled controls: values captured for each scheduled simulation step. Discrete Replay actions instead request individual operations and receive an accepted or refused result. The current Godot driver submits dash as Action{kind=.Dash, aim=direction}. A versioned dash_schedule() selects receipt-time delivery for dash and turret mount/release; other actions retain scheduled timing. Receipt-time delivery queues a valid request for the next available authority tick in per-seat order; the client's proposed tick does not choose that execution time. The comparison fixture explicitly chooses receipt timing for every action and disables the classifier in its isolated game copy.

T captures a generation-checked turret target for mount/release through the same action-intent helper. Aim/fire operate the mounted turret; movement, dash, revive and casting are blocked until dismount. See shared turret.

The driver captures a dash direction once it has a readable player state, keeps the request through queue-capacity or recovery delays, and clears it only after issue_action returns a sequence ID. Sampling movement/fire cannot consume that pending request. The lobby, spectators, typing and menus discard unsubmitted input, and holding Shift while leaving an overlay does not manufacture a new press. A request during an unreadable interval remains latched until the driver can capture its direction.

The reusable action-intent helper owns the copied payload, pending tickets and recovery bookkeeping. Tickets include their epoch, so a reused sequence after migration cannot consume an old result.

After queue admission the normal action ledger owns delivery. The driver tracks confirmed outcomes by sequence, removing each tracked ID once. A game rejection is a result, not an instruction to retry the dash automatically. dash_probe exposes submitted, confirmed, refused and pending counts for diagnostics. Dash effects use the existing speculative event and correction/cancellation path.

The authority still checks connection, yard membership, health and cooldown. Direction is bounded and normalized; zero direction uses the player's current facing. Actions run after the movement step, so their dash expiry includes ten future movement ticks. The legacy control path starts its ten ticks immediately. Both use dash_start, the same speed, cooldown, event identity and counter rules.

Control.dash remains a compatibility field for already-recorded scheduled inputs in earlier Replay saves. The current authored driver never sets it. Its presence does not give those historical inputs receipt-time delivery or a new action verdict. This preserves their original execution semantics during import and replay while the new input path uses explicit action results.

Content 47 introduced the Dash enum member and timing contract. The converter paths for content 42–47 use frozen old action enums and preserve world state, pending action IDs/ticks, recorded controls and assets. A newly loaded game does not silently reinterpret an older save; use the explicit converter described in saves.

The stress-fire development helper uses the same local origin as ordinary input: predicted position on a client, current authoritative position on a host. Its nearest-target census still uses the authoritative enemy observation. This does not add line-of-sight filtering, target leading, damage changes or guaranteed hits; cover and stale enemy observations can still produce misses.

RSY_SNAPSHOT_EVERY=N (browser query snapshot_every=N) sets the requested snapshot interval in simulation ticks, clamped to 1..30 (default 3). Simulation remains at 60 Hz; three ticks requests 20 snapshots per second. Actual delivery also depends on backpressure, loss and recipient budgets. This is a local delivery preference, not a change to gameplay speed or saved world content.

Content 48 introduced authority-only rewind history without changing dash timing. The save guide records current content and accepted conversion inputs.
